Read the source diff of 25de257. F1 and F2 of review-28 are addressed. Blocks (MEDIUM, rule 6): adminRuntime cookieRestore now calls tokenStore.clear('admin') in its catch for any CSRF-recovery failure, outages included; the wrapped admin store's clear also drops persisted held writes, so an admin who reloads during a network or backend outage loses a held write with an unknown outcome and can re-submit it under a new key. Before 25de257 an outage at reload kept the hold (review-23 design: holds bound to the admin survive a null restore). Fix: clear only when the error is not an outage, as readCookieSession already does; same rule for the client restore. LOW residual: if B finishes signing in while T1's client CSRF response (as A) is in flight, T1 stores A over B, T2 ends instead, and T1 reads B's data under A's name until the next 401 (at most the access-token lifetime); admin is covered by the getAdminSession compare. Record, no fix.
